blocks.text: Probation is a two-way period to confirm that the role is right for you and that you are right for the role, and to give you the support you need to succeed.
Your probation length is stated in your contract. It is {{policy.default_probation_months}} months unless your contract says otherwise.
Your manager will agree objectives with you in your first weeks, hold regular one-to-ones and arrange the training you need.
Reviews take place on the dates in your probation schedule. Any concerns are raised early, with examples and a fair chance to improve.

items: An extension, where your contract and the law allow it, with clear reasons and objectives.
Ending your employment after a fair review.

blocks.text: If you are absent for a significant part of your probation, it may be extended where your contract and the law permit, so that you have a fair opportunity to show what you can do.
Being on probation does not remove your legal rights, including protection from discrimination.
Questions about this policy go to {{policy.contact}}.

This policy explains how we work. Unless your contract says otherwise, it does not form part of your contract of employment and we may update it from time to time, following any consultation the law requires. Nothing in this policy reduces your rights under the law or any applicable collective agreement.
If you have questions or concerns about this policy, speak to your manager or {{policy.contact}}. You will not be treated unfairly for raising a genuine concern.
